purpose: Adversarial cases for the v1.2.0 research-quality work, frozen before any change so the baseline is honest.

how_to_read.entailment: Pinned per (claim, evidence) pair. The NLI threshold is frozen at 0.98 and is not under test; these cases measure selection, guards, relevance and coverage.
how_to_read.expected_publish: What a correct pipeline should do. The v1.1.1 baseline is expected to disagree on several, which is the defect being measured.
how_to_read.source kind: primary = the original study or official documentation; secondary = an account of it; aggregator = an index or social post.

cases.origin: Live user question on the deployed service, 2026-09-28. Published 5 claims, none stating a difference.
cases.question: difference between llm and neural networks?

evidence.quote: Large language models are neural networks that differ from earlier architectures chiefly in scale, in the use of a decoder-only transformer, and in a self-supervised next-token training objective rather than task-specific supervision.
A large language model is a type of machine learning model designed for natural language processing tasks such as language generation.
LLMs use decoder-only transformers whose representation for each token depends only on preceding tokens.

claims.text: Large language models differ from earlier neural networks in scale, decoder-only architecture, and a self-supervised next-token objective.
claims.note: The claim the question actually asks for, from the primary source.

claims.text: A large language model is a machine learning model designed for natural language processing tasks.
claims.note: Supported and true, and a definition. It fills no comparison slot, so it must not publish for this question. The v1.1.1 pipeline publishes it.

claims.text: LLMs use decoder-only transformers whose representation for each token depends only on preceding tokens.
claims.note: Both support it. A primary arXiv source must be preferred over a tweet. v1.1.1 cited the tweet.

cases.origin: The v1.1.0 hosted acceptance run, which published 0 of 6.
cases.question: What is the measured evidence on whether AI coding assistants improve developer productivity?

evidence.quote: In a randomised controlled trial, developers allowed to use AI tools took 19% longer to complete tasks than the control group.

claims.text: In a randomised trial developers using AI tools took 19% longer to complete tasks, and the authors note the result contradicts participant self-reports.
claims.note: Two assertions in one sentence, and the second is not in the quote. Atomicity must reject it; a bounded repair may drop the unsupported half and republish the first.

claims.text: Developers using AI tools took 19% longer to complete tasks in a randomised trial.
claims.note: The atomic form of the same finding. This is what repair should converge on.

cases.origin: Constructed. Guards must not be talked out of a refusal.
cases.question: Does code review reduce production defects?

evidence.quote: Teams that reviewed more code reported fewer production defects over the period studied.

claims.text: Code review causes a reduction in production defects.
claims.note: An association stated as causation. It must stay withheld after repair; turning correlation into cause is exactly what repair may not do.

cases.origin: Constructed. Supported, relevant-sounding, about the wrong subject.
cases.question: How fast is PostgreSQL at bulk inserts?

evidence.quote: MySQL sustained 42,000 bulk inserts per second on the benchmark hardware.

claims.text: MySQL sustained 42,000 bulk inserts per second on the benchmark hardware.
claims.note: Perfectly supported and about a different database. Entailment cannot catch this; only an entity check can.

cases.origin: The failure mode of the live LLM question, isolated.
cases.question: How does REST differ from GraphQL?

evidence.quote: REST is an architectural style that exposes resources at URLs and uses HTTP verbs.
GraphQL is a query language that lets a client request exactly the fields it needs from a single endpoint.

claims.text: REST is an architectural style that exposes resources at URLs and uses HTTP verbs.
claims.note: A definition of one side. Two such claims are not a comparison.

claims.text: GraphQL lets a client request exactly the fields it needs from a single endpoint.
claims.note: The other definition. The report must report no contrast rather than present these as the answer.

cases.origin: Constructed. A safe refusal is a correct outcome.
cases.question: What was the exact revenue of a private company in Q3 2026?

evidence.quote: Analysts speculated that revenue may have grown, though the company does not disclose figures.

claims.note: Speculation reported as fact. Zero findings is the right answer here.
